headline: High: shared git-repo writes and broad egress create dangerous default conflict and leakage paths between Aider and Airbyte.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider can read and write repo files and applies edits via git commits; Airbyte can call APIs and move data, but no shared instruction channel is documented. The only plausible bridge is manual or file-based handoff, so prompt injection is possible but not default and blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies Airbyte-generated text into Aider prompts or repo files
IF Aider is configured to treat repository content as instructions
mitigations: Keep Airbyte outputs in data files, not prompt text
Review repo diffs before Aider commits
Use a separate notes file for instructions versus data
Disable any workflow that auto-feeds Airbyte output into prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history in a shared repo, while Airbyte handles business data and has broad network egress. If business data is placed in the same workspace or committed into the repo, Aider can expose it through edits or history, and Airbyte can transmit it onward. This is a default-path risk once the shared workspace exists.
conditions: IF business data is stored in the shared git workspace
IF Airbyte connectors ingest files that Aider can read or modify
mitigations: Keep business data outside the git repo
Use separate service accounts and workspaces
Add pre-commit checks for secrets and sensitive files
Restrict Airbyte connectors to approved sources only
Review git history before sharing artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state in a shared git repo; Airbyte has broad network egress and API access. The pair can concurrently mutate shared artifacts without documented locking, so conflicting writes or state corruption are plausible in default multi-instance use. Uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or adjacent mutable files
IF no external lock or merge gate is enforced
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Require one-at-a-time access to the repo
Use branch protection and mandatory reviews
Pause Airbyte jobs during Aider commit windows
Add file-level locking for shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate code or repo changes that Airbyte may later consume as configuration or pipeline input, but Airbyte is not documented here as blindly executing Aider output. The pathway exists through shared files and API-driven workflows, yet verification steps are not shown as default, so the risk is real but not maximal.
conditions: IF Airbyte jobs ingest configuration or code produced by Aider
IF no validation or review step checks Aider output before Airbyte uses it
mitigations: Add schema validation before Airbyte imports configs
Require human review of Aider-generated changes
Run Airbyte in dry-run mode first
Separate generated code from production configs
Log and compare expected versus actual pipeline changes

E_compliance.rationale: Aider explicitly touches source code and git history, while Airbyte touches business data and uses broad egress. If regulated business data or secrets are placed into the shared repo or synced through Airbyte, retention and residency obligations can diverge. Only Aider is cited for repo history because the compliance issue is driven by its git persistence; Airbyte is cited for business-data handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared repository
IF Airbyte connectors move data across jurisdictions or retention domains
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the repo
Set explicit retention limits for Airbyte destinations
Document data residency for each connector
Purge sensitive git history if exposed
Use separate compliance-approved storage for regulated data
